text:
[verdict]
In the 50 retrieved historical episodes where the tape looked like BABA on 2026-09-18, the median 5-session forward return was 0.05%, with outcomes split exactly 50% above and 50% below zero. The single number to anchor on is that median of 0.05%: this state historically produced no directional edge over a one-week horizon, only wide dispersion.

[state]
The engine retrieved these analogs because BABA's current state is defined by deep underperformance and distance from highs. The most distinctive features are its distance from the 52-week high at -41.23% (z-score -1.798), a 20-session return of -13.25% (z-score -1.442), and a 20-session return versus benchmark of -13.37% (z-score -1.459). Elevated 20-session realised volatility at 42.99% (annualised) and a WTI crude change of 19.24% over 20 days also shaped the neighborhood. The earnings proximity feature (dte) is capped at 45 days, so the engine cannot isolate an immediate pre-earnings setup; it treats this as a generic 45-day window. Macro conditions show a VIX level of 15.44, a 10y-2y Treasury slope of 0.25, and a Fed funds target change of 0.25 bp over 90 days. Equity market sentiment sits at a score of 57.1 in the "Greed" band, though the CNN Business Fear & Greed cross-check reads 38.3 ("fear"), driven by extreme fear in stock price strength (0.8) and breadth (0.8). For context on this symbol right now, Yahoo Finance · BABA headlines include "Alibaba Stock Falls. Treasury Yields Aren’t Just a U.S. Problem" and "Chinese AI Chips Could Flood the Market. Alibaba’s New Chip Is 3X Better Than Its Predecessor." The crypto sentiment reading of 70 ("Greed") applies only to the separate crypto market and the tokenised wrapper venue, not to BABA's equity mood.

[history]
Across the 50 analogs, the mean 5-session return was 0.96%, but the median was just 0.05% with a standard deviation of 6.64%. The distribution is slightly positively skewed (0.321), bounded by a minimum of -20.44% and a maximum of 21.43%. Exactly 50% of the episodes finished above zero and 50% below. The 10th percentile was -4.76% and the 90th percentile was 7.87%. The bad tail is dominated by specific recent sessions: AVGO on 2026-09-08 returned -7.95%, META on 2026-08-13 returned -8.26%, and NKE on 2026-09-03 returned -5.08%. Conversely, the upside tail includes NIO on 2025-07-08 returning 21.43% and INTC on 2025-08-11 returning 14.58%. Notably, BABA itself appeared twice in the retrieval set; the closest BABA analog from 2026-09-08 returned -2.95%. China ADR peers JD and PDD from early September 2026 returned -3.54% and -4.68% respectively.

[tails]
A position can end near flat while being un-holdable intra-week. The median max adverse excursion across the 50 analogs was -2.11%, while the median max favourable excursion was 2.87%, yielding a reward-to-risk ratio of 1.36. In terms of breach probabilities, 24% of the analog paths breached a 5% drawdown during the 5-session horizon. A 10% drawdown was breached in 2% of the paths, a 15% drawdown in 2%, and a 20% drawdown in 2%. The 10th percentile of max adverse excursion was -5.89%, meaning in 1 out of 10 similar states, the path dipped nearly 6% against the entry before the week was over.

[stress]
The baseline median return is 0.05%. Several stress scenarios materially worsen that picture. The 2020-02/03 liquidity crash scenario produced a median forward return of -4.32% (delta -4.37% vs baseline), with a 52.1% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown; caveat: central-bank backstops arrived inside the window, so the realised rebound is baked into the forward returns, and it is a sample of one regime, not a forecast. The 2025-04 tariff shock scenario yielded a median of -3.8% (delta -3.85%), with a 42.3% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown; caveat: policy reversals inside the window make the tail asymmetric in a way specific to that episode. The 2018-Q4 tightening scare produced a median of -3.26% (delta -3.31%); caveat: it ended with a policy pivot in January 2019, which flatters late-window analogs. The 2022 inflation/rate bear scenario showed a median of -3.32% (delta -3.37%); caveat: a nine-month window means the per-date cap of 2 analogs samples it repeatedly, so treat it as a regime description, not 50 independent events. The earnings release day scenario resulted in a median of -0.95% (delta -1.0%); caveat: earnings dates for foreign private issuers come from 6-K full-text search and are noisier than 8-K Item 2.02 dates. The weekend hold on the 7x24 venue scenario produced a median of -0.2% (delta -0.25%); caveat: blocks are paired to analogs by index modulo the block count, a deterministic convention, not a joint distribution, and a perpetual carries funding and basis a spot token does not. No scenarios were skipped.

[reasoning]
The three scenarios most relevant to buying BABA into earnings are: first, the earnings release day scenario, because it directly conditions on known-event sessions, showing a median of -0.95% (delta -1.0%) across 50 analogs with a 12% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown. Second, the 2025-04 tariff shock, because it isolates trade-exposed China-linked cash flows, producing a median of -3.8% (delta -3.85%) across 26 analogs with a 30.8% probability of falling more than 10%. Third, the 2020-02/03 liquidity crash, because it represents the worst-case forced-deleveraging tail, yielding a median of -4.32% (delta -4.37%) across 48 analogs with a 52.1% breach probability. A reader should distrust the heavy concentration of analogs from 2025 (23 sessions) and 2026 (16 sessions), which dominate the 50-analog set and compress the historical regime diversity. No scenario contradicts the direction of a long idea outright—the baseline median is positive at 0.05%—but the earnings-day and tariff-shock medians are negative, offering no historical support for a reliable upward move.

[limits]
This analysis has concrete limits. The engine's honest verdict states: "Analog retrieval hits its coverage target out of sample and its width tracks each instrument's own volatility, but it is NOT sharper than a same-name unconditional band at matched coverage, and its raw PIT distribution fails a uniformity test. It is a stress-testing and provenance instrument, not an alpha source." The directional hit rate is 50.1%. The conformal interval achieves 80.8% out-of-sample coverage, but the matched coverage sharpness versus the same-name unconditional benchmark is -7.6%, meaning the naive benchmark is tighter. For path risk validation, at the stated 10% drawdown level, the realised breach rate out of sample was 2%, while the mean predicted rate from the analog excursion share was 3.4%. The calibration gap is 1.4 percentage points with a clustered standard error of 0.48 pp. The analog Brier MAE is 0.0196, compared to 0.0241 for the volatility reflection benchmark, 0.024 for the same-name calibration, and 0.021 for the pooled calibration. The paired Brier confidence intervals resolve the analog's superiority over all three benchmarks, as none of the 95% intervals span zero (e.g., vs vol reflection: -0.0071 to -0.0022). Regarding the wrapper, status is "measured". The primary venue is Bitget official MCP (BABA/USDT, RWA perpetual futures). The reference cash market is shut for 81.4% of the week, and 67.32% of the wrapper's own hourly movement landed in those closed hours. It is a "tight" tracker with a return correlation of 0.9781 and tracking error of 60 bp/day. The basis band is -0.19% to 0.67%, and the spread is 5.34 bps. Caveat: a tight perpetual is not the underlying and not a redeemable spot token; it carries idiosyncratic risk and funding, and nothing here feeds the retrieval engine or conformal scale. For the return layer measured on Bitget, across 6 distinct weekend starts (pooled across 39 instruments, so effective sample size is 6 weekends, not 233 blocks), the median weekend block return was -1.185%, the 10th percentile was -1.7235%, standard deviation was 1.647%, and the median intra-weekend adverse excursion was -1.551%. The share of weekends breaching a 5% drawdown was 16.7%. These are wrapper returns measured while the reference market was shut and are NOT the retrieved outcome distribution above, which is built on 5x24 daily sessions.
